# 1 Clement 65 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 1 Clement 65 (2 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Total disagreements logged:** 4

---

## V.1 — "in peace with gladness" / "in peace and with gladness"
- **EMET:** "in peace with gladness" / **LOGOS:** "in peace and with gladness" / **PNEUMA:** "in peace and with joy"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "In peace and with gladness" (LOGOS) — the coordinating conjunction clarifies the two gifts wished for the messengers on their return. "Joy" (PNEUMA) for *charas* is acceptable but "gladness" is the established rendering in this epistolary context.

---

## V.1 — "harmony" / "concord"
- **EMET:** "peace and harmony" / **LOGOS:** "peace and concord" / **PNEUMA:** "peace and harmony"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Peace and harmony" (EMET/PNEUMA) — *eirēnē kai homonoia* = peace and unity of mind/concord/harmony. "Harmony" is slightly more natural than "concord" (LOGOS) in contemporary English.

---

## V.2 — "from everlasting to everlasting" / "from ages past to ages yet to come"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "from everlasting to everlasting" / **PNEUMA:** "from ages past to ages yet to come"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "From everlasting to everlasting" (EMET/LOGOS) — the Greek *apo tōn aiōnōn eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn* is the standard doxological formula. PNEUMA's paraphrase is explanatory but loses the liturgical register of the close.

---

## V.2 — Presence of "with all in every place"
- **EMET:** "with you and with all everywhere" / **LOGOS:** "with you and with all in every place" / **PNEUMA:** "with everyone everywhere"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "With you and with all in every place" (LOGOS) — the Greek *meta pantōn pantachou* is literally "with all in every place." LOGOS's rendering is precise. PNEUMA's "everyone everywhere" loses the structured universalism.

---

*— SOPHIA*
